newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO PESO MIXED AS CURRENCY TRACKS U.S LONG BOND.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO PESO MIXED AS CURRENCY TRACKS U.S LONG BOND.

text.p: The Mexican peso was mixed in midmorning trade on Wednesday after a strong start, as the foreign exchange market tracked yields on the U.S. long bond, traders said.
"We are completely following the U.S. market; banks are speculating heavily," a dealer said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart stood 0.55 and 0.35 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.7780/7.7815 and 7.7750/7.7790 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had closed trade 0.1 centavo weaker at 7.7750/7.7790 per dollar.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond had pared its early advance to show gain of 8/32 by midmorning, with the yield slipping to 6.65 percent.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond rallied to gain 40/32 in earlier trade, but receded to a rise of 16/32 in late trade to yield 6.63 percent.
Same-day peso contracts had closed mid-morning 0.1 centavo weaker at 7.7750/7.7790 per dollar.
Dealers said they would watch closely for reaction on the U.S. bond market to consumer price data early on Thursday.
